- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a forecast drop, it often overshoots; cap peak forecast or add a downward correction buffer.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes; apply lagged smoothing or reduce sensitivity to last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean reversion bias toward 30-day rolling average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, adjust early days downward if sentiment is weak or upward if sentiment is strong.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.80” patterns, model often misreads sentiment; use sentiment as a multiplier (e.g., 0.8 = 80% weight on sentiment signal).
